plan.notes: University of Denver is on the quarter system (Fall/Winter/Spring); term_system=quarter. Official sample 4-year course plan ('Bachelor of Science in Physics and Astronomy') from the 2025-2026 Undergraduate Bulletin Physics and Astronomy program PDF (12 quarters). VARIABLE-CREDIT RECONCILIATION: the bulletin lists MATH 2070 as 0-4 credits and PHYS 3995 as 1-10 credits (twice, Fourth Year Fall and Spring) and declares 'Total Credits: 183-198'. Encoded at the representative full values — MATH 2070 = 4, PHYS 3995 = 4 each quarter — which reconciles every variable term total to within the bulletin's stated ranges (Y2 Winter 14 within 10-14; Y4 Fall 10 within 7-16; Y4 Spring 16 within 9-18) and yields a degree total of 190, inside the bulletin's declared 183-198. Declared total 190 = plan's actual sum; fixed term totals (Y1 18/17/17, Y2 17/14/17, Y3 16/14/18, Y4 10/16/16) reconcile exactly. Generic slots (language sequences, AI/SI requirements, PHYS electives, minor/concentration blocks, study-abroad block) encoded as choice slots exactly as the official plan lists them; no courses invented. BS requires 60 total PHYS credits including one PHYS elective. Footnote 1: BIOL 1010/1020 or BIOL 1011/1021 may be taken instead of CHEM 1010 and CHEM 1240. Footnote 2: Analytical Inquiry-Society and Scientific Inquiry-Society courses may be taken in any order. Footnote 3: PHYS 3510/3520 and PHYS 3611/3612 offered every other year; PHYS 3111/3112 and PHYS 3841 in the alternating years; either set may be taken first. Footnote 4: one PHYS elective required for the 60 PHYS credits; graduate-level courses with permission. Footnote 5: BS students will often enroll in PHYS 3991 Independent Study or PHYS 3995 Independent Research as part of senior thesis work; credits are variable. Third Year Fall is the bulletin's recommended study-abroad quarter.
